memory_update.text: Conversion may be the tightest commercial bottleneck, but clean public exposure appears limited; Honeywell/ConverDyn is relevant for mapping, not a pure-play candidate.
Centrus Energy should remain the primary public reference candidate for domestic enrichment and HALEU in this node.
BWX Technologies should remain on the map for advanced fuel fabrication/TRISO, but later layers must test materiality versus defense and nuclear-services revenue.
Energy Fuels is an underfollowed second-order upstream candidate: domestic uranium feedstock exposure is real, but it is not the same bottleneck as conversion, enrichment, or HALEU.

node: Nuclear fuel cycle: uranium, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, fabrication
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the nuclear fuel-cycle node finds that investable exposure is unusually sparse beyond uranium miners. The strongest chokepoint signals are conversion, enrichment/HALEU, and advanced fuel fabrication. Centrus is the clearest public enrichment/HALEU name; Honeywell is the buried U.S. conversion exposure through Metropolis Works/ConverDyn but is too diversified to be a clean expression; BWX Technologies is a public advanced fuel/TRISO fabrication exposure but is already relatively visible and larger-cap; Energy Fuels is a smaller U.S.-listed upstream uranium supplier that may provide second-order domestic fuel-cycle exposure, though it is less directly tied to conversion/enrichment bottlenecks.
